source_blocks.html:
参考范文

The cartoon captures a familiar campus scene. In front of a billboard advertising various lectures, a girl complains to her friend, "They're not related to our major, so they won't help our study." Her companion replies, "Go and listen; there's bound to be some benefit."

Simple as it is, the picture reflects a prevalent mindset: some students limit themselves strictly to their own discipline and dismiss knowledge from other fields. Yet in an era of rapid change, those with broad horizons and multiple skills adapt far better and prove more competitive. As the saying goes, knowledge is never a burden. Cross-disciplinary learning not only sparks creativity but may also become the very key to solving problems within one's major.

From my perspective, we should cultivate the habit of lifelong, wide-ranging learning. Universities ought to encourage students to explore diverse possibilities, for only by staying hungry for knowledge can we grow into versatile talents.

【译文】

漫画捕捉了一个熟悉的校园场景。在一块满是各类讲座信息的广告牌前，一名女生对同伴抱怨："又不是我们专业的，听了也没多大用。"同伴却答道："去听一下，肯定有好处。"

画面虽简单，却折射出一种普遍心态：一些学生把自己严格局限在本专业之内，轻视其他领域的知识。然而在快速变迁的时代，视野开阔、技能多元的人适应力更强，也更具竞争力。常言道，艺多不压身。跨学科学习不仅激发创造力，更可能成为破解本专业难题的关键。

在我看来，我们应培养终身、广博学习的习惯。大学应鼓励学生探索多样可能，因为唯有保持对知识的饥渴，我们才能成长为复合型人才。

paragraphs.html: People often grumble that plastics are too durable. Water bottles, shopping bags, and other trash litter the planet, from Mount Everest to the Mariana Trench, because plastics are ubiquitous and don't break down easily. But some plastic materials change over time. They crack and frizzle. They "weep" out additives. They melt into sludge. All of which creates huge headaches for institutions, such as museums, trying to preserve culturally important objects. The variety of plastic objects at risk is dizzying: early radios, avant-garde sculptures, celluloid animation stills from Disney films, David Bowie costumes, the first artificial heart.

paragraphs.html: So van Oosten and colleagues at RCE began to study ways to protect polyurethane. First, they took foam samples similar to the nature carpets and infused some with stabilizing and consolidating chemicals that modern manufacturers often use. Van Oosten calls those chemicals "sunscreens" because their goal was to prevent further light damage and rebuild worn polymer fibers. Then the team used xenon lamps to artificially age both treated and untreated samples, and examined them under high-powered microscopes. The results were encouraging. Samples that lacked sunscreen had withered under the barrage of photons: The molecular "struts" shoring up the foam were 42% thinner and notably more brittle than before the lamp treatment. The struts in samples with sunscreen decreased by as little as 12.5%. Armed with that knowledge, conservators working with RCE infused several Gilardi sculptures, including two nature carpets, with the sunscreen to stabilize them. People often grumble that plastics are too durable. Water bottles, shopping bags, and other trash litter the planet, from Mount Everest to the Mariana Trench, because plastics are ubiquitous and don't break down easily. But some plastic materials change over time. They crack and frizzle. They "weep" out additives. They melt into sludge. All of which creates huge headaches for institutions, such as museums, trying to preserve culturally important objects. The variety of plastic objects at risk is dizzying: early radios, avant-garde sculptures, celluloid animation stills from Disney films, David Bowie costumes, the first artificial heart.

人们常常抱怨塑料太耐用了。从珠穆朗玛峰到马里亚纳海沟，水瓶、购物袋和其他垃圾散落地球，因为塑料无处不在且不易分解。但有些塑料材料会随时间变化。它们开裂、卷曲。它们"渗出"添加剂。它们融成污泥。所有这些都给博物馆等试图保护具有重要文化意义物品的机构带来了巨大麻烦。面临风险的塑料制品种类令人眼花缭乱：早期收音机、先锋派雕塑、迪士尼电影的赛璐璐动画剧照、大卫·鲍伊的服装、第一颗人工心脏。

Certain artifacts are especially vulnerable because some pioneers in plastic art didn't always know how to mix ingredients properly, says Thea van Oosten, a polymer chemist who, until retiring a few years ago, worked for decades at the Cultural Heritage Agency of the Netherlands (RCE). "It's like baking a cake: If you don't have exact amounts, it goes wrong," she says. "The object you make is already a time bomb."

荷兰文化遗产局（RCE）的聚合物化学家西娅·范·奥斯滕（几年前退休）说，某些手工艺品尤其脆弱，因为一些塑料艺术先驱并不总是知道如何正确混合原料。"这就像烤蛋糕：如果用量不精确，就会出错，"她说，"你制作的物品已经是一颗定时炸弹。"

And sometimes, it's not the artist's fault. In the 1960s, the Italian artist Piero Gilardi began to create hundreds of bright, colorful foam pieces. Those pieces included small beds of roses and other items as well as a few dozen "nature carpet" — large rectangles decorated with foam pumpkins, cabbages, and watermelons. He wanted viewers to walk around on the carpets — which meant they had to be durable.

而有时，这并非艺术家的错。20世纪60年代，意大利艺术家皮耶罗·吉拉尔迪开始创作数百件色彩鲜艳的泡沫作品。这些作品包括小束玫瑰和其他物品，以及几十块"自然地毯"——用泡沫南瓜、卷心菜和西瓜装饰的大长方形地毯。他希望观众能在地毯上走动——这意味着它们必须耐用。

Unfortunately, the polyurethane foam he used is inherently unstable. It's especially vulnerable to light damage, and by the mid-1990s, Gilardi's pumpkins, roses, and other figures were splitting and crumbling. Museums locked some of them away in the dark.

paragraphs.html: Millennials were told that if you did well in school, got a decent degree, you would be set up for life. But that promise has been found wanting. As degrees became universal, they became devalued (just as governments hiked up the cost of getting one). Education was no longer a secure route of social mobility. Today, 28 per cent of graduates in the UK are in non-graduate roles; a percentage which is double the average amongst the OECD.

As the latest crop of students pen their UCAS form and weigh up their options, it may be worth considering just how the point, purpose and value of a degree has changed and what Gen Z (and their parents) need to consider as they start the third stage of their educational journey.

当最新一批学生填写大学申请表、权衡各种选择时，或许值得思考一下：学位的意义、目的和价值发生了怎样的变化，以及Z世代（及其父母）在开启教育旅程第三阶段时需要考虑什么。

Millennials were told that if you did well in school, got a decent degree, you would be set up for life. But that promise has been found wanting. As degrees became universal, they became devalued (just as governments hiked up the cost of getting one). Education was no longer a secure route of social mobility. Today, 28 per cent of graduates in the UK are in non-graduate roles; a percentage which is double the average amongst the OECD.

千禧一代被告知，如果你学业优异、拿到体面的学位，这辈子就有保障了。但这一承诺被证明是欠缺的。随着学位变得普及，它贬值了（正如政府推高了获得学位的成本）。教育不再是可靠的社会流动途径。如今，英国28%的毕业生从事着非毕业生岗位；这一比例是经合组织平均水平的两倍。

This is not to say that there is no point in getting a degree, but rather stress that a degree is not for everyone, that the switch from classroom to lecture hall is not an inevitable one and that other options are available.

这并不是说拿学位毫无意义，而是要强调学位并不适合所有人，从课堂到阶梯教室的转变并非不可避免，还有其他选择。

Thankfully, there are signs that this is already happening, with Gen Z seeking to learn from their millennial predecessors, even if parents and teachers tend to be still set in the degree mindset. Employers have long seen the advantages of hiring school leavers who often prove themselves to be more committed and loyal employees than graduates. Many too are seeing the advantages of scrapping a degree requirement for certain roles—just as Penguin did in 2016.

值得庆幸的是，有迹象表明这已经在发生，Z世代试图从千禧一代前辈那里吸取教训，即使父母和老师往往仍固守学位思维。雇主早就看到了招聘中学毕业生的好处——他们往往比毕业生更敬业、更忠诚。许多雇主也看到了取消某些岗位学位要求的好处——就像企鹅兰登书屋在2016年所做的那样。

For those for whom a degree is the desired route, consider that this may well be the first of many. In this age of generalists, it pays to have specific knowledge or skills. Postgraduates now earn 40 per cent more than graduates. When more and more of us have a degree, it makes sense (albeit expensive) to have two.

It is unlikely that Gen Z will be done with education at 18 or 21; they will need to be constantly up-skilling throughout their career to stay agile, relevant and employable. It has been estimated that this generation due to the pressures of technology, the wish for personal fulfillment and desire for diversity will work for 17 different employers over the course of their working life and have five different careers. Education, and not just knowledge gained on campus, will be a core part of Generation Z's career trajectory.

I have often heard older generations talk about their degree (even if it was gained decades ago) in the present and personal tense: "I am a geographer or 'I am a classicist'". Their sons or daughters would never say such a thing; it's as if they already know that their degree won't define them in the same way.

paragraphs.html: One example of how artists and scientists have together rocked the senses came last month when the Sydney Symphony Orchestra in Australia performed a reworked version of Antonio Vivaldi's The Four Seasons. paragraphs.html: More than half a century ago, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) opened its Center for Advanced Visual Studies (CAVS) in Cambridge to explore the role of technology in culture. The centre was established during the Vietnam War, when many scientists in the United States were being criticized for working on defence contracts. Its founders believed that artists and scientists could, together, create a vision for a more humane world. They deliberately focused their projects around light — hence the 'visual studies' in the name. Light was something that both artists and scientists had an interest in, and therefore could form the basis of collaboration, says Seth Riskin, a visual-arts researcher at the MIT Museum who previously worked at CAVS.

Scientists are increasingly seeking out visual artists and designers to help them to communicate their work to new audiences. One example of how artists and scientists have together rocked the senses came last month when the Sydney Symphony Orchestra in Australia performed a reworked version of Antonio Vivaldi's The Four Seasons. The work was entitled The (Uncertain) Four Seasons, and variations of the score containing local data were sent to every major orchestra in the world. The performance was a creative call to action ahead of November's United Nations.

The premise was that the common law of contract lacked sufficient safeguards for workers against arbitrary conduct by management. Long gone are the days when a boss could simply give an employee contractual notice.

个人申诉程序旨在保护普通工人的工作免受"不当解雇"。其前提是普通合同法缺乏足够保障，使工人免受管理层任意行为的侵害。老板只需简单给员工合同通知就解雇人的日子早已一去不复返。

But these provisions create difficulties for businesses when applied to highly paid managers and executives. As countless boards and business owners will attest, constraining firms from firing poorly performing, high-earning managers is a handbrake on boosting productivity and overall performance. The difference between C-grade and A-grade managers may very well be the difference between business success or failure. Between preserving the jobs of ordinary workers or losing them. Yet mediocrity is no longer enough to justify a dismissal.

但这些条款在适用于高薪经理和高管时给企业带来了困难。无数董事会和企业主可以证明，限制公司解雇表现不佳、收入丰厚的经理，就像给提高生产率和整体业绩踩了手刹。C级经理和A级经理之间的差距，很可能就是企业成败的差距。就是保住普通工人工作还是失去它们的差距。然而，平庸已经不足以成为解雇的理由。

Consequently — and paradoxically — laws introduced to protect the jobs of ordinary workers may be placing those jobs at risk.

因此——而且矛盾的是——为保护普通工人工作而出台的法律，可能正在将这些工作置于风险之中。

If not placing jobs at risk, to the extent employment protection laws constrain business owners from dismissing underperforming managers, those laws act as a constraint on firm productivity and therefore on workers' wages. Indeed, in "An International Perspective on New Zealand's Productivity Paradox" (2014), the Productivity Commission singled out the low quality of managerial capabilities as a cause of the country's poor productivity growth record.

即使不将工作置于风险之中，在就业保护法限制企业主解雇表现不佳经理的范围内，这些法律也会制约企业生产率，从而制约工人工资。事实上，在《新西兰生产率悖论的国际视角》（2014）中，生产力委员会特别指出管理能力低下是该国生产率增长不佳的一个原因。

Nor are highly paid managers themselves immune from the harm caused by the ERA's unjustified dismissal procedures. Because employment protection laws make it costlier to fire an employee, employers are more cautious about hiring new staff. This makes it harder for the marginal manager to gain employment. And firms pay staff less because firms carry the burden of the employment arrangement going wrong.

高薪经理本身也不能免于ERA不当解雇程序造成的伤害。因为就业保护法增加了解雇员工的成本，雇主在招聘新员工时更加谨慎。这使得边缘经理更难找到工作。而且公司给员工的工资更低，因为公司承担了雇佣安排出错的负担。

Society also suffers from excessive employment protections. Stringent job dismissal regulations adversely affect productivity growth and hamper both prosperity and overall wellbeing.

社会也因过度的就业保护而受损。严格的解雇法规对生产率增长产生不利影响，并阻碍繁荣和整体福祉。

Across the Tasman, Australia deals with the unjustified dismissal paradox by excluding employees earning above a specified "high-income threshold" from the protection of its unfair dismissal laws. In New Zealand, a 2016 private members' Bill tried to permit firms and high-income employees to contract out of the unjustified dismissal regime. However, the mechanisms proposed were unwieldy and the Bill was voted down following the change in government later that year.

partb_options.head: Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–G

options.label: A
options.en: Zoos which spare no effort to take care of animals should not be subjected to unfair criticism.
options.zh: 不遗余力照料动物的动物园，不应遭受不公正的批评。

options.label: B
options.en: To pressure zoos to spend less on their animals would lead to inhumane outcomes for the precious creatures in their care.
options.zh: 迫使动物园减少对动物的投入，会给它们所照管的珍贵生灵带来不人道的后果。

options.label: C
options.en: While animals in captivity deserve sympathy, zoos play a significant role in starting young people down the path of related sciences.
options.zh: 尽管圈养动物值得同情，但动物园在引导年轻人走上相关科学之路上发挥着重要作用。

options.label: D
options.en: Zoos save people trips to wilderness areas and thus contribute to wildlife conservation.
options.zh: 动物园让人们省去前往荒野的奔波，从而有助于野生动物保护。

options.label: E
options.en: For wild animals that cannot be returned to their natural habitats, zoos offer the best alternative.
options.zh: 对于无法回归自然栖息地的野生动物，动物园提供了最佳的替代方案。

options.label: F
options.en: Zoos should have been closed down as they prioritize money making over animals' wellbeing.
options.zh: 动物园早该关闭，因为它们把赚钱置于动物福祉之上。

options.label: G
options.en: Marris distorts our findings which actually prove that zoos serve as an indispensable link between man and nature.
options.zh: 马里斯歪曲了我们的研究结果——而研究恰恰证明，动物园是人与自然界之间不可或缺的纽带。
